cards.back: A device that **detects a change in its environment** and converts a **physical phenomenon into a measurable signal** (usually analog voltage). The 'eyes and ears' of IoT.

**Transducer** = any energy converter (superclass). **Sensor** = transducer on the input side (physical→electrical, measures). **Actuator** = transducer on the output side (electrical→physical, acts).

**Active** = emits its own energy and measures the reflection (ultrasonic, radar, LiDAR); needs power, works in dark. **Passive** = detects natural energy already present (thermocouple, LDR, PIR); low power.

cards.front: Is a PIR sensor active or passive? Why?
cards.back: **Passive** — it detects the infrared **heat radiated by bodies**; it emits nothing. (An active IR sensor would emit an IR beam.)

**Invasive** = inserted into/part of the system, direct measurement, high accuracy but disturbs system (thermocouple in cylinder, pH probe). **Non-invasive** = external, indirect, easy/safe (IR thermometer, clamp-on flowmeter).

**Accuracy** = close to the **bullseye** (true value). **Precision/repeatability** = darts **clustered together** (consistent), even if in the wrong spot. Precise-but-inaccurate = systematic error you can calibrate out.
**Sensitivity** = output change **per unit input** (the slope, e.g., 10 mV/°C). **Resolution** = the **smallest input step** the sensor can detect (e.g., 0.01°C). Different properties.
**Offset (bias)** = non-zero output when input is zero (fixed by auto-zero). **Drift** = slow change in output over time/temperature for a fixed input (fixed by recalibration).
Accuracy, precision/repeatability, sensitivity, resolution, linearity, range (full-scale), offset, drift.
Time for a sensor to react to a **step change** and settle within a defined % (typically **90% or 95%**) of its final value. Critical for real-time apps.
**Response time, SNR (signal-to-noise ratio), bandwidth (Hz), frequency response.** Matter for fast-changing apps (robotics, vibration, audio).
**Frequency response** = full curve of gain & phase vs input frequency. **Bandwidth** = width of the usable flat part of that curve (in Hz). Outside it, readings distort.

**Measurement requirement** (what/range/resolution), **performance** (accuracy/response), **environment** (waterproof/UV/temp), **power** (battery/solar), **cost** (scale), **integration** (analog/digital, I²C/SPI, MCU compatibility).

cards.front: Why is sensor selection a 'constraint-satisfaction' problem?
cards.back: The most accurate sensor is useless if it drains a solar node, costs too much to scale, or outputs a bus the MCU can't read. You find the sensor satisfying **all** constraints — often 'good-enough, cheap, low-power' wins.
A device that **converts an electrical signal into a physical action** (motion, sound, light, heat) — the 'doer'/'hands' of IoT that acts on the environment.
**Electric** (servo/stepper), **Hydraulic** (pressurised fluid), **Pneumatic** (compressed air), **Thermal** (heat expansion), **Magnetic** (electromagnets/relays).
**Open-loop** = no feedback, fixed command (fire-and-forget, e.g., timed sprinkler). **Closed-loop** = uses sensor feedback to self-correct (e.g., thermostat, blinds following a light sensor).

A sensor integrating **sensing element + signal conditioning + ADC + microcontroller + comms interface** → outputs a clean **digital** value, often **self-calibrating**. Edge intelligence at the sensing element.
**IEEE 1451** = smart-transducer standard. **TEDS** (Transducer Electronic Data Sheet) = on-board memory holding the sensor's identity + calibration → **plug-and-play** self-describing sensors.

cards.front: Defining capabilities of a smart object?
cards.back: **Unique identity**, **sensing**, **processing** (MCU+memory), **communication** (network-addressable), **actuation & logic** — senses AND acts autonomously.
**Mobility**: static (thermostat) vs mobile (wearable/asset tracker). **Reporting frequency**: low (monthly rust sensor) vs high (vibration sensor at hundreds of Hz).
**Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems** — miniaturized mechanical+electrical elements (micro→mm scale) **microfabricated on silicon** via photolithography. Made sensing tiny, cheap, low-power.

cards.front: MEMS examples + what an IMU is?
cards.back: Accelerometer (tilt/acceleration), gyroscope (rotation), pressure, microphone, magnetometer. An **IMU** = MEMS accelerometer + gyroscope (+ magnetometer).
Combining data from **multiple sensors** to produce a **more accurate/complete/reliable** estimate than any single sensor alone.

cards.front: Why fuse accelerometer + gyroscope in an IMU?
cards.back: **Complementary flaws**: accelerometer is **noisy but drift-free**; gyroscope is **smooth but drifts**. Fusing (complementary/Kalman filter) gives orientation that's both smooth AND stable.
**Complementary** (different aspects → full picture), **Competitive/redundant** (same quantity → fault tolerance, e.g., voting), **Cooperative** (derive new info, e.g., stereo cameras → depth).
**Complementary filter** (lightweight high-pass gyro + low-pass accel) and the **Kalman filter** (optimal predict–correct estimator; **EKF** for non-linear systems like GPS+IMU).
**Offset** (zero-input bias), **gain/scale** error, **non-linearity**, and **drift** over time. Found by comparing to a known reference and adjusting.

cards.front: One-point vs two-point vs multi-point calibration?
cards.back: **One-point** fixes offset; **two-point** fixes offset + gain (e.g., 0°C ice & 100°C boiling); **multi-point** also fixes non-linearity via a curve.

cards.front: Why does self-calibration matter for IoT?
cards.back: Sensors are deployed **at scale, unattended, for years** where drift accumulates and manual recalibration is impractical. Auto-zero / internal references / temp compensation keep data reliable.

cards.front: What is a WSN and its node components?
cards.back: **Wireless Sensor Network** = low-power sensor nodes reporting to a **sink/gateway**. Each node: **sensor(s) + microcontroller + radio transceiver + battery/energy harvester**.

**WSN** = a **subset** of IoT — sensing + basic (usually **unidirectional**) data transmission. **IoT** = full **bidirectional** ecosystem: sensing, processing, actuation, analytics, control, cloud integration.
**Low power/compute** (long battery life), **self-organizing** (ad-hoc mesh/tree), **unattended operation**. Communication is **event-driven** or **periodic**.
**Flexible/wearable** (e-skin), **bio/chemical** (glucose, lab-on-chip), **energy-harvesting/self-powered** (Green IoT), **nano-sensors/smart dust**, **AI-embedded (TinyML)**.
They scavenge ambient energy (light, vibration, heat) → **no battery** → sustainable, maintenance-free deployment of **billions** of nodes. Removes IoT's biggest bottleneck (power) = **Green IoT**.
**Task-specific**, **real-time**, **resource-constrained** (limited memory/compute), **often no OS or an RTOS**, tightly coupled to hardware.
**MCU** = CPU **+ memory (flash/RAM) + peripherals** (GPIO/timers/ADC/comms) on **one chip** → ideal for IoT. **Microprocessor** = just the core, needs external RAM/storage/peripherals.
**Setup once** (configure clocks, GPIO, peripherals) then a **super-loop** `while(1)` that runs forever (sense→process→act). Arduino's `setup()`/`loop()` is this pattern.
A family of **32-bit ARM Cortex-M** microcontrollers by **STMicroelectronics**. Series: **F1** (general), **L** (ultra-low-power), **F4** (high-performance, FPU/DSP).
Blocks: **CPU, Flash, SRAM, GPIO, Timers, ADC, USART/I²C/SPI**. Toolchain: **IDE → compiler/assembler → linker (.bin) → programmer/flasher (ST-Link) → debugger (GDB/OpenOCD)**.
GPIO modes: **Input, Output, Alternate Function, Analog**. Blink: `HAL_GPIO_TogglePin(GPIOC, GPIO_PIN_13)` + `HAL_Delay(500)` in the super-loop (HAL hides raw registers; CubeMX generates setup).
**Sense** (ADC/I²C) → **Process** (Cortex-M) → **Act** (GPIO/PWM actuator) → **Transmit** (UART → Wi-Fi/BLE/cellular module → cloud) → **repeat** (sleep to save power).
